item.title: Charges filed against activists who posed as Minnesota voters
item.description: Activists who call themselves the Citizen Justice League said they were testing Minnesota's 53-year-old voter voucher law. Videos from the August primary showed them claiming to be registered voters.

item.title: Graham, Andrews tied in South Carolina Senate race, new poll shows
item.description: Mike Nellis, former senior advisor to Vice President Kamala Harris, and Mike Hahn, former deputy digital director of the National Republican Senatorial Committee, join "The Takeout" to discuss the upcoming midterms, RFK Jr. and more.

item.title: Florida Congress candidate Bale Dalton on his campaign, hopes of flipping open seat
item.description: Bale Dalton, a candidate for Florida's 7th congressional district, joins "The Takeout" to discuss his campaign and hopes of flipping his district's open seat in the upcoming midterms.

item.title: Watch: Democratic candidate Brad Lander on his ban from Israel, Senate race
item.description: Brad Lander, a Democratic congressional nominee from New York, joins "The Takeout" to discuss his recent detention in the West Bank and the upcoming midterms.

item.title: Dolores Huerta, activist who stood behind farmers and Latinos, dies at 96
item.description: Labor and civil rights activist Dolores Huerta has died at 96. CBS News' Ed O'Keefe has more on that and on the state of midterm races in Alaska.

item.title: Watch: Michigan voters discuss Senate race
item.description: Senate candidate Abdul El-Sayed is trying to push as many Democrats to the polls as possible, as 1.2 million early votes have already been cast in Michigan. CBS News' Aaron Navarro has the details.

item.title: Former President Obama campaigns for Democrats in Georgia ahead of midterms
item.description: Former President Obama is preparing to hit the road in Georgia as the midterms approach. CBS News' Skyler Henry has more.

item.title: Trump stumping for Republican candidates in Ohio ahead of midterms
item.description: President Trump is in Ohio to push for Republican candidates with less than a week to go before the midterms. Nikole Killion reports.

item.title: Why is France on Fire? With Thomas Chatterton Williams
item.description: The worst violent protests in years expose France's stagnant economy and its romance with revolt. Thomas Chatterton Williams says the country is on a knife's edge. If you'd like to share your own great question, email us at greatquestion@cbsnews.com.

item.title: "Your vote is your voice": A look at why voting matters
item.description: Why is it important to vote even if the president isn't on the ballot? House and Senate control, governor's mansions, ballot questions and more that will be determined by the 2026 midterm elections.

item.title: Cruise ship Villa Vie Residences suspends operations in Cambodia due to rising fuel cost
item.description: Villa Vie, a U.S. cruise ship that touted its cabins as floating homes, suspended its three-year voyage in Cambodia due to fuel costs, forcing hundreds of passengers to disembark. CBS News' Cristian Benavides has more.

item.title: SPLC alleges DOJ is treating witness as a member of prosecution team
item.description: The group's lawyers are asking a judge to let them subpoena a former SPLC informant who has been voluntarily providing material to the government.

item.title: Federal reserve holds interest rates steady despite high inflation
item.description: The Federal Reserve held interest rates steady on Wednesday after raising borrowing costs in September to clamp down on inflation. CBS News' Kelly O'Grady breaks it down.

item.title: Experts react to new findings on CTE in former NFL players
item.description: A new study from Boston University looks at the rate of the brain disease CTE in former NFL players who died between 2008 and 2023.

item.title: Fed holds interest rates steady even as inflation remains high
item.description: The U.S. central bank left borrowing costs unchanged this month after hiking rates in September for the first time in three years.

item.title: Watch: Voters speak about sense of discouragement ahead of midterms
item.description: CBS News' Riley Callanan spoke to potential voters who voiced their sense of discouragement ahead of the upcoming midterm elections.

item.title: AI company aims to make confusing local government easier to understand
item.description: Approximately $2 trillion of economic activity flows through local government every year. Many of those decisions are made in public meetings, though few people attend. A new tech company, Hamlet, is using AI to summarize public information and make local government easier to understand. Its founder, Sunil Rajaraman, joins CBS News to discuss.

item.title: Caregivers face soaring costs, taking a toll on income and jobs
item.description: Caregivers spend an average of $11,500 per year looking after an aging parent, relative or friend, up roughly 60% since 2021, according to AARP.

item.title: Lawyers question case against ex-FBI officials over Hunter Biden probe
item.description: Defense attorneys for two former FBI counterintelligence officials accused of lying to Congress raised doubts about the strength of the evidence and the motives behind the charges.

item.title: How Ramaswamy's attack ad against Acton is swaying Ohio voters' preferences
item.description: President Trump is on a campaign blitz six days ahead of the midterm elections that will determine control of Congress. Republican strategist Rina Shah and Democratic strategist Robyn Patterson join CBS News to discuss the controversial Ohio race attack ad.

item.title: Flávio Bolsonaro leaves Brazil, lands in U.S. after election loss
item.description: Flávio Bolsonaro, who lost Brazil's presidential election, left the country with his family and State Department official told CBS News they would receive U.S. visas.

item.title: High-speed train crash in Spain kills at least 68, dozens injured
item.description: Dozens of people were killed or injured when a high-speed train crashed into another train in central Spain, officials said.

item.title: Midterm campaigns make final push as early voters hit the polls
item.description: Election Day is Tuesday, Nov. 3, and early voting is underway throughout the country.

item.title: Dolores Huerta, labor activist and civil rights icon, dies at 96
item.description: Dolores Huerta was a labor activist and civil rights leader who co-founded the group that later became the United Farm Workers.

item.title: Hayden Panettiere's death ruled accidental by South Carolina police
item.description: A South Carolina coroner previously confirmed Panettiere died from an accidental drug overdose that included fentanyl.

item.title: Apple's first foldable phone broke within hours, some owners say
item.description: "I didn't even make it through setup," one consumer said after his new iPhone Duo cracked shortly after he bought it.

item.title: Ted Cruz calls El-Sayed a "jihadist leprechaun" at campaign stop
item.description: At a campaign event outside of Detroit, GOP Sen. Ted Cruz of Texas attempted to tie Democratic candidate Abdul El-Sayed to the Muslim Brotherhood.

item.title: No clear winner in Israeli election as polls suggest stalemate
item.description: Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu appears to have won fewer votes than his main challenger, according to early exit polls, but both sides will likely struggle to cobble together a coalition.

item.title: 10/27: The Takeout with Major Garrett
item.description: Israel saw a record-shattering turnout in its parliamentary elections; Flávio Bolsonaro fled Brazil to the U.S. after his election defeat.

item.title: Labor activist Dolores Huerta says Trump "does not know history"
item.description: Longtime labor activist Dolores Huerta says President Trump's disparaging remarks about Mexicans show he "does not know history," and called on Latinos in California, Texas and other states to push for change.
